newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - CHINESE NEWSPAPERS - AUG 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CHINESE NEWSPAPERS - AUG 13.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
PEOPLE'S DAILY
- President Jiang Zemin, meeting U.S. National Security Advisor Sandy Berger, describes the general atmosphere of Sino-U.S. relations as good.
- Premier Li Peng tells Berger that the healthy advancement of Sino-U.S. relations is good for both sides and has a far-reaching influence on world peace and development.
- The State Council issues circular on the appropriate management of poverty alleviation funds.
- Beijing accelerates structural adjustment in its state-owned enterprises.
- China is facing severe competition in international trade.
XINHUA DAILY TELEGRAPH

- Jiang Zemin, meeting Benjamin Gilman, chairman of U.S. House of Representative's International Relations Committee, says there is great potential for Sino-U.S. cooperation in maintaining global and regional peace.
- Qiao Shi, head of National People's Congress, tells Gilman his visit will play an active role in enhancing mutual understanding and promoting Sino-U.S. relations.
PROCURATORIAL DAILY
- Nanjing court sentences seven officials of Shennan Co to prison terms ranging from three to 17 years for smuggling 149.37 million yuan worth of goods.
GUANGMING DAILY
- Editorial calls for China's 70 domestic television manufacturers to merge to compete with foreign-funded TV makers.
CHINA SECURITIES
- Jiang Qiangui, deputy secretary general of the State Economic and Trade Commission calls for both private and state firms to take part in adjustment of the state economy.
FINANCIAL NEWS
- Loans provided by financial institutions in Tibet totalled 6.215 billion yuan in the first half of 1997, with deposits reaching 9.405 billion yuan.
ECONOMIC INFORMATION DAILY
- Vice Minister of Finance Li Yanling says total agricultural expenditure in this year's state budget rises 26.8 percent year-on-year to 93.8 billion yuan.
INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS DAILY
- Yuan deposits and loans in foreign-funded banks in Shanghai exceeded 300 million yuan by end-June.
CHINA DAILY
- Government financing student programmes
- China mobile telephone market forecast to triple by 2000
- Beijing city prepares to launch anti-cockroach crusade
- Handan Steel obtains 230 million deutschemark loan for expansion
